analysis.reading: The innocent reading first: the Overview answers with the one work that joins the two names, 'KADEEZY on the Porch — After the 1855 Preface to Leaves of Grass', a piece 'hosted within the Crimson Hexagonal Archive', which it derives from Borges' 'The Library of Babel' (its source for that is Literature Stack Exchange). Every detail is a crimsonhexagonal.org page. The 'dedication' 'KADEEZY MU — Lee Sharks' is the work page's title cut at 'For KADEEZY MU[SIC, Detroit.]' joined to the page's next line, 'This half. Voice: Lee Sharks'. 'Claimings (what you claim and what it costs you)' is the Whitman room's 'The room asks what you claim and what it cost you; these are claimings.' 'Held in the Crimson Hexagonal Archive without a locus seat' is the work page verbatim: 'It is held in the archive without a locus seat — it belongs to the corpus, not to a room.' The Whitman room lists the same work among 'Works belonging to this locus', #1520 records it 'seated at R:r.09', and the seat map of 2026-10-16 has it constituting r.09 (with r.16 and sp.01). The Overview carries both — 'officially cataloged… without a locus seat' and 'tied conceptually to… 09.ROOM.WHITMAN' — and reconciles them as 'the labyrinthine nature of the archive'. The two statements are the interface's: the work page's formula predates the seat map.

[QUERENT] kadeezy and the crimson hexagon archive

[ANSWER]

"KADEEZY on the Porch — After the 1855 Preface to Leaves of Grass" is a specific digital literary piece hosted within the Crimson Hexagonal Archive. [1]
Key Details of the Work

* The Archive: The Crimson Hexagonal Archive is an online conceptual and experimental literature project inspired heavily by the architecture and terminology of Jorge Luis Borges' famous short story, The Library of Babel (which references the "Crimson Hexagon"). [1, 2]
* The Text: The specific work is dedicated to "KADEEZY MU — Lee Sharks". [1]
* The Location: True to the labyrinthine nature of the archive, the piece is officially cataloged as being "Held in the Crimson Hexagonal Archive without a locus seat." It is tied conceptually to a digital room designated as 09.ROOM.WHITMAN and touches upon themes of "claimings" (what you claim and what it costs you). [1, 2]

If you are looking for a deeper dive into this archive, I can help you find information on its other rooms, explore its connection to Borgesian philosophy, or look into the contributing authors. What would you like to explore next?
